subtle.$description: Inset zones, striped rows, panels flush with the page

muted.$description: A visibly deeper recessed fill than subtle — the AppShell content-slot backdrop the screen sits on

overlay.$description: Modal / drawer scrim — the darkener behind a centered modal. Pure black at 40% (was a zinc-950 tint at ~70%; lightened + de-tinted so the interface stays readable behind the modal). `color.modal.scrim` aliases this.

overlay-subtle.$description: Neutral hover/press wash — layers on top of whatever's underneath instead of replacing it (row hover, list-item hover, etc.), unlike background.subtle which is an opaque swap

default.$description: Primary button, active nav item, selected state

brand-subtle.$description: Tinted brand fill: selected row, info banner

warning-strong.$description: Orange alert accent — the warning pill/icon in the alert system, distinct from amber warning

warning-strong-subtle.$description: Orange warning/attention pill fill (matches the other -subtle tones at 100)

card.$description: Card fill — warm near-white #fcfcfc (product override, not on the Tailwind scale)

raised.$description: Surface carrying an elevation shadow: popover, dropdown

inverse.$description: The one surface that stays dark regardless of theme — Tooltip's fill.

subtle.$description: Body text — the default reading colour for paragraphs and UI copy

muted.$description: Muted / de-emphasised text — hints, placeholders, timestamps, captions

brand-solid.$description: Text that must read as the same accent as a solid brand fill nearby (a bar, a dot) — aliases background.brand.default itself, not a hand-picked shade, so the two can never drift apart. NOT for text on a light/subtle background — text.brand (700) stays there; this is ~100 lighter and won't clear AA on brand-subtle.

success-solid.$description: Text matching a solid success fill nearby — see brand-solid.

warning-solid.$description: Text matching a solid (amber) warning fill nearby — see brand-solid. Not warning-strong (orange) — that hue is scoped to the alert-pill system only.

danger-solid.$description: Text matching a solid danger fill nearby — see brand-solid.

on-success.$description: Text on color.background.success — added alongside on-brand/on-danger for SegmentedControlItem's tone fills; same white-on-solid-mid-tone pattern.

highlight.$description: White edge highlight for glass / raised surfaces (asymmetric top-left catch)

highlight-active.$description: Glass edge highlight when the surface is focused/active — a full 1.5px primary border that replaces the white top-left catch

category.$description: A general-purpose named-hue set for badge labels / settings cells / anything needing an arbitrary category identity color, distinct from color.chart.* (data-series identity) and color.badge.* (fixed status vocabulary: neutral/brand/success/warning/danger). Validated with the dataviz skill's validate_palette.js in ADJACENT-only mode (same rigor as color.chart.*, relaxed from an earlier --pairs all pass that only found 6 safe hues — module/badge colors don't have a chart's fixed legend order, but a --pairs-all bar was judged stricter than needed here). ALL CHECKS PASS in the object-key order below — that order is not incidental, it's the validated sequence (brand/teal/rose/lime/fuchsia/cyan/pink/violet/emerald/blue): any consumer that auto-assigns 'the next category color' (a picker, a round-robin tagger) MUST cycle through them in this order, not alphabetically or by insertion into some other list — reordering can reintroduce an adjacent clash this pass specifically ruled out (e.g. teal directly next to cyan, or pink next to rose, both tested and rejected). 3 of the 10 (teal, cyan, lime) trade contrast for distinctness (2.9-3.3:1 vs. own-100, short of 4.5:1) — accepted because a category color is always paired with a visible label, satisfying the skill's 'secondary encoding' exception the same way the CVD floor-band findings below are. Consumed by Tag (text only) and CategoryIcon (text/background/background-muted) — this is deliberately capped at these 10 hues, not the larger 16-color set `CategoryIcon`'s Figma predecessor ("Colored icons") used; the extra 6 (sky/indigo/purple/green/yellow/taupe) were never validated for CVD/contrast here and were dropped rather than carried forward unvetted. `background` added 2026-09-14 for CategoryIcon's `emphasis=strong` (modules) — deliberately reuses the exact same primitive as `text` (not a new shade): the two are used as opposite roles (colored-text-on-white vs. white-icon-on-color), and contrast is symmetric between a color pair regardless of which side is foreground, so the already-validated `text` contrast ratio carries over unchanged. `background-muted` added the same day for `emphasis=muted` (settings, 'just slightly less saturated and accented than default') — a first pass tried each hue's pale `.100` tint (matching the `color.background.brand-subtle` precedent) but that read as a completely different treatment (pale fill + colored icon) rather than a gentler version of the same one; a plain lighter Tailwind step (e.g. .700→.600) was tried next and rejected too — Tailwind ramps often get MORE saturated approaching their chroma peak (~400-500) while getting lighter, the opposite of the ask, confirmed by inspecting each hue's own HSL saturation across steps. `background-muted` is instead a **first-of-its-kind exception to this file's alias-only convention** (there's no existing raw-hex precedent to point to here — flagging that plainly rather than overstating it): each hue's `background` value converted to HSL, saturation reduced by a flat 0.20 (hue and lightness held fixed so contrast barely moves), converted back to hex — carries its own explicit `$type` since there's no alias chain for Style Dictionary to infer one from. Verified against a white icon on top: worst case (lime) is 3.74:1, comfortably above the 3:1 UI-graphics floor, every other hue clears 4.1-6.9:1. Recompute with the same method (S -= 0.20, H/L fixed) if `background` ever changes for a hue.
